To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the NMDA antagonist, argiotoxin‐636, is a subunit‐specific blocker of NMDA receptors; and (ii) the NR2B subunit is more sensitive than the NR2A and C subunits, and the NR2C subunit is more resistant to argiotoxins than the NR1 and NR2A subunits.
argiotoxin 636 is a subtype‐specific blocker of NMDA receptors, and that the toxin interacts with the pore forming TM2 domain of NMDA receptor.

the NMDA receptors of the NR1–NR2A type are more susceptible to argiotoxins than those of the NR1-NR2C type and this difference is caused by the presence of an argiotoxin‐binding site at the putative pore-forming TM2 region of NR2A, but not NR2C, subunits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the molecular mechanisms underlying argiotoxin 636 action.
the molecular mechanism of argiotoxin‐636‐induced blockade of NMDA receptor‐channels.
the molecular mechanism of the argiotoxine‐induced block of the cloned NMDA receptor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
argiotoxin 636 blocks all NR1‐NR1, NR1‐ NR2B and NR2C‐NR2C NMDA receptor homomers and heteromers with a similar potency.
argiotoxin 636 interacts with a common site in the TM2 domain of the NMDAR subunits, but with a different efficacy.
argiotoxin 636 blocks the NMDA‐activated ion channel in a subunit‐specific and voltage‐dependent manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the argiotoxins are a family of potent blockers of NMDA receptor‐like cation channels, and that they interact with the pore forming TM2 segment of the receptor.
argiotoxin‐sensitivity is determined by the amino acid residue at the Q/R site in the TM2‐domain.
the NR1‐ NR2A and the NR1‐N2B NMDA receptors are blocked by argiotoxins, whereas NR1‐NR1C receptors are insensitive to the toxins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NMDAR subunit NR2A is a target for argiotoxin 636, a toxin that blocks NMDARs by interacting with a conserved amino acid in the TM2 domain.
argiotoxin 636 is a useful tool to study the structure and function of NMDA receptors.
argiotoxin‐636 is a useful pharmacological tool for studying NMDAR subunit composition and function in native tissues.
